access_notes.value: Access requires a Snowflake account; the docs link a self-serve trial for getting started. There is no separate 'API plan' — credentials (OAuth integration, key-pair JWT, or programmatic access token) are created inside the account, and usage is consumption-billed at rates that vary by edition (Standard, Enterprise, Business Critical, VPS).
access_notes.quote: The Snowflake Edition that your organization chooses determines the unit costs for the credits and the data storage you use.

api_versioning_or_deprecation_notes.value: Reviewed docs state the REST API reference reflects the latest API version; APIs are under active development and expanding. No formal versioning scheme or deprecation/sunset policy was found in the supplied evidence.
api_versioning_or_deprecation_notes.quote: The Snowflake REST APIs reference documentation reflects the latest version of the Snowflake REST APIs.

verdict_reason: Snowflake documents generally available REST APIs with roughly 49 resource groups plus a SQL API, all on public docs.snowflake.com pages. Credentials are self-serve: a trial account is documented and OAuth, key-pair JWT, and programmatic access token auth are all documented. Consumption billing applies, but it does not gate a developer from obtaining working API access.
open_questions: OAuth scopes/permissions documentation was not captured in the supplied sources; verify whether Snowflake documents scope values for OAuth integrations.
Webhooks: CREATE NOTIFICATION INTEGRATION (webhooks) pages appeared in search results but were not included in SOURCES, so webhook support is unconfirmed here.
Sandbox/test environment: only a getting-started trial account is evidenced; a limited-access 'Cortex sandboxes' page appeared in search results but was not fetched.

Rate limits: a search snippet for the Cortex Agents page mentions 1,000 requests per minute per account with a 500-request burst, but that page is not in SOURCES and snippets are not citable; rate_limits left unverified.
The Snowflake-managed MCP server is per-account (no single public endpoint is published), so the documentation URL is used in place of an endpoint.

SDK list is limited to the drivers captured in the quoted block (Go, JDBC, .NET, Node.js); the same page also lists ODBC, PHP PDO, Python, Spark, and Snowpark/Scala connectors that were not included in a single verbatim quote.
